source.title: How to set up your Next.js project for AI coding agents
source.description: Learn how to configure your Next.js project so AI coding agents use up-to-date documentation instead of outdated training data.

source.title: Project structure and organization
source.description: Learn the folder and file conventions in Next.js, and how to organize your project.

source.title: Layouts and Pages
source.description: Learn how to create your first pages and layouts, and link between them with the Link component.

source.title: Linking and Navigating
source.description: Learn how the built-in navigation optimizations work, including prefetching, prerendering, and client-side navigation, and how to optimize navigation for dynamic routes and slow networks.

source.title: Server and Client Components
source.description: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.

source.title: Fetching Data
source.description: Learn how to fetch data and stream content that depends on data.

source.title: Caching
source.description: Cache Components with `use cache`: caching data or UI, streaming uncached data in Suspense, runtime APIs, static shell prerendering, and prefetching.

source.title: Font Optimization
source.description: Self-host Google and local fonts with next/font to avoid layout shift and requests to Google, applied app-wide via the root layout.

source.title: Image Optimization
source.description: Serve resized, lazy-loaded images with next/image: local and remote sources, width and height to stop layout shift, remotePatterns allowlisting.

source.title: Proxy
source.description: Formerly Middleware: run code before a request completes to rewrite, redirect or modify headers, scoped by a matcher; not for full auth.

source.title: Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)
source.description: Learn how to cache and revalidate data using fetch options, unstable_cache, and route segment configs for projects not using Cache Components.

source.title: How to optimize your Next.js application for production
source.description: Recommendations to ensure the best performance and user experience before taking your Next.js application to production.

source.title: Testing
source.description: Learn how to set up Next.js with four commonly used testing tools — Cypress, Playwright, Vitest, and Jest.

source.title: How to set up Jest with Next.js
source.description: Learn how to set up Jest with Next.js for Unit Testing and Snapshot Testing.

source.title: How to set up Playwright with Next.js
source.description: Learn how to set up Playwright with Next.js for End-to-End (E2E) Testing.

source.title: How to set up Vitest with Next.js
source.description: Learn how to set up Vitest with Next.js for Unit Testing.

source.title: use cache
source.description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.

source.title: use cache: private
source.description: Learn how to use the "use cache: private" directive to cache functions that access runtime request APIs.

source.title: use cache: remote
source.description: Learn how to use the "use cache: remote" directive for persistent, shared caching using remote cache handlers.

source.title: use client
source.description: Learn how to use the use client directive to render a component on the client.

source.title: use server
source.description: Learn how to use the use server directive to execute code on the server.

source.title: generateMetadata
source.description: Learn how to add Metadata to your Next.js application for improved search engine optimization (SEO) and web shareability.

source.title: redirect
source.description: Redirect with a 307 from components, Route Handlers or Server Actions; why it must sit outside try/catch and can't run in event handlers.

source.title: permanentRedirect
source.description: Redirect with a 308 from Server and Client Components, Route Handlers or Server Actions, choosing push or replace history behaviour.

source.title: loading.js
source.description: Instant loading UI while a route segment streams via Suspense; why no fallback shows for layouts reading runtime data, and soft 404s.

source.title: Metadata Files API Reference
source.description: Favicon, icon, Open Graph image, robots.txt, sitemap and manifest as static or code-generated files, and excluding them from the Proxy matcher.

source.title: Font Module
source.description: Every next/font option such as weight, subsets, display and variable, plus multiple fonts, Tailwind CSS variables and a shared font definitions file.

source.title: TypeScript
source.description: Next.js provides a TypeScript-first development experience for building your React application.

source.title: next.config.js
source.description: Write the config as CommonJS, ESM or TypeScript, or as an async function per build phase, and unit test its redirects and rewrites.

source.title: devIndicators
source.description: Configuration options for the on-screen indicator that gives context about the current route you're viewing during development.

source.title: redirects
source.description: Map old paths to new ones in next.config.js: 307 vs 308, wildcard and regex matching, header, cookie and query conditions.

source.title: serverComponentsHmrCache
source.description: Configure whether fetch responses in Server Components are cached across HMR refresh requests.

source.title: Turbopack
source.description: Turbopack is an incremental bundler optimized for JavaScript and TypeScript, written in Rust, and built into Next.js.

source.description: PLACEHOLDER

source.description: PLACEHOLDER

source.title: How to use fonts
source.description: Pages Router: self-host Google and local fonts with next/font in pages/_app to avoid layout shift and requests to Google.

source.title: ESLint Plugin
source.description: Learn how to use and configure the ESLint plugin to catch common issues and problems in a Next.js application.

source.title: create-next-app
source.description: Create Next.js apps using one command with the create-next-app CLI.
